To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the analytic web is a formal representation of the scientific process used in the creation of a dataset that meets the two key criteria for dataset reliability, and (2 ) the Little-JIL process definition language can be used to precisely and accurately represent the scientific processes involved in the creation of environmental datasets.

(1) an analytic web is an effective way to ensure the reliability of a dataset; (2) the use of an appropriate process definition language (e.g., Little-JIL) is essential for the construction of an analytic web; (3) an analytic web can be constructed from existing data and metadata; (4) an analytic web provides a complete audit trail and detailed process metadata that describe the scientific process that produced the dataset.

(1) a scientific process can be modeled as an analytic web, a formal representation of the process that includes a complete audit trail and detailed process metadata; (2) an analytic web can be constructed from an existing scientific process using a high-level process language (Little-JIL) and existing tools for data analysis; and (3) the resulting analytic web provides a complete record of all artifacts and activities involved in the creation of a dataset, and thus can be used to evaluate the dataset for reliability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of creating reliable environmental datasets.
the creation of a formal representation of scientific process that can be used as a foundation for a new generation of tools and methods for data analysis and dataset reliability.
ensuring reliable datasets for environmental science.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper describes a new approach to representing the scientific process of creating datasets, an approach that can be used to ensure dataset reliability and that has the potential to yield significant benefits to the science of environmental modeling.
the use of an Analytic Web to represent the scientific processes used to create environmental datasets will ensure the reliability of those datasets.
the proposed approach will enable the scientific community to create and use more reliable datasets for environmental research, modeling, and forecasting.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing the infrastructure to enable the scientific community to make the best use of the data that is being collected.
the analytic web is a powerful tool for ensuring the reliability of environmental datasets.
we are developing a framework that allows us to represent the scientific processes used to create datasets, and to evaluate the quality of these processes and of the datasets themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analytic web approach provides a means for scientists and managers to create datasets that meet the requirements of reproducibility and analyzability.
the analytic web is a useful and practical approach to the problem of dataset reliability, and can be readily integrated into existing tools and metadata standards.

the analytic web approach provides a means to ensure the reliability of datasets, and hence the reliability of environmental models and forecasts, in an era where the amount of data available to scientists is increasing exponentially.
